sources.quote: It runs 448 km from Phongsaly Province to Luang Prabang Province.

reference.note: The itinerary refers to the river valley of the Nam Ou seen from a waterfall trail on a Pakbeng-Luang Prabang cycling loop; the valley itself is unambiguous, exact viewpoint is not. Coordinates are Nong Khiaw (Wikipedia) as a representative point.

sources.quote: Phase I of the dams, including Nam Ou 2, Nam Ou 5, and Nam Ou 6 began operating on May 12, 2016.

facts.rationale: Supported by Wikipedia (Nam Ou river cascade dams): seven-dam cascade, phase I operating 2016, phase II c.2020. numeric=true because the fact states a dated period ('the 2010s'), which falls under the date rule.

sources.quote: Phase I of the dams, including Nam Ou 2, Nam Ou 5, and Nam Ou 6 began operating on May 12, 2016.

sources.quote: The river rises in Muang Ou Nua near the Lao-Chinese border
It flows north to south through three provinces: Phongsaly, Oudomxay, and Luang Prabang

facts.rationale: Resolved to supported. Focus on the Global South (whose Ou River report Wikipedia cites) states verbatim that the river flows through Phongsaly, Oudomxay and Luang Prabang. B's counter-evidence (dams only in Phongsaly/Luang Prabang; no OSM segment found) does not state the river's course and no T1 source contradicts the Oudomxay claim; Wikipedia's '448 km from Phongsaly Province to Luang Prabang Province' gives only the endpoints. Moderate confidence.
